transcript.content: Hi, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, yeah… nice to meet you too. I guess the main thing that kind of pushed me to come in is my eating’s been really off lately. It’s probably not a huge deal, but some days I’ll realize I basically skipped meals without meaning to, and then other nights I’m up late just going through takeout or snacks after midnight. It’s been a little embarrassing, honestly, and I figured I should probably talk to someone about it.
When that late-night eating happens, do you feel unable to stop or control how much you’re eating?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say it’s totally out of control or anything, but there are nights where once I start, it’s like I just keep going through the takeout or snacks and then I’m kind of surprised how much I ate. Other days I barely eat at all, so it’s just been… all over the place, I guess. That’s kind of what scared me into coming in, if that makes sense.
After those nights when you eat a lot, do you ever make yourself vomit?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve felt gross or guilty after, but I haven’t made myself throw up or anything like that.
During those late-night episodes, do you eat an unusually large amount of food for the situation?

Yeah… I guess for the situation, probably yes. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but some nights after midnight I’ll be going through takeout and snacks, and then afterward I’m like, “Okay, that was more than I really meant to eat.” It’s just kind of all over the place, because other days I’ll forget meals completely.
After those nights when you eat a lot, do you ever try to make up for it by fasting, exercising a lot, or using laxatives?

Um… not really, no. I mean, I might tell myself the next day, like, “Okay, maybe eat lighter,” but I’m not doing, like, laxatives or trying to work out a ton to cancel it out. I don’t think it’s that kind of thing. Is that what you mean?
When those late-night eating episodes happen, do you feel like you can’t stop eating once you’ve started?

Yeah… sometimes it feels that way, I guess. Not like every time, and I don’t want to make it sound like I’m totally out of control, but once I start with takeout or snacks late at night, I can kind of keep going past the point I meant to stop. Then other days I barely remember to eat, so it’s just been really all over the place.
Do these late-night eating episodes upset you a lot?

Yeah… I mean, I try not to make a huge deal out of it, but it does bother me. Honestly, the eating being so all over the place is part of what scared me into coming in. Some days I’ll forget meals completely, and then other nights I’m tearing through takeout and snacks after midnight, and afterward I feel kind of embarrassed and worried, like, “What am I doing?” Is that… the kind of upset you mean?
About how often do these late-night eating episodes happen?

I don’t know if I’ve counted exactly… maybe a few nights here and there? It’s not every single night. But it’s enough that I noticed, like, some days I’ll basically forget meals, and then other nights after midnight I’m just going through takeout and snacks. That pattern is what kind of scared me, honestly.
On average, do these late-night eating episodes happen at least once a week?

Yeah… I think probably at least once a week, give or take. I haven’t tracked it or anything, but the thing that scared me is my eating’s been all over the place—some days I’ll forget meals completely, and then other nights I’m up after midnight going through takeout and snacks. I know that probably sounds bad… but yeah, I’d say weekly.
How long has this pattern of late-night overeating been going on?

I guess… it’s been long enough that I noticed it as a pattern, not just one bad night. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but honestly that’s kind of what scared me into coming in—my eating’s been all over the place. Some days I’ll forget meals completely, and then other nights I’m tearing through takeout and snacks after midnight.
Has this pattern been going on for at least 3 months?

I’m not totally sure it’s been a full three months… I haven’t really kept track like that. It’s just been long enough that I started noticing it and got worried, you know? Like, some days I barely eat or forget meals, and then other nights I’m up after midnight going through takeout and snacks. I don’t want to exaggerate it, but it has felt like a pattern.
Has your weight gotten low enough that you or other people have been concerned you’re underweight?

Not really low like that, no… I don’t think anyone’s looked at me and said I’m underweight. It’s more that my eating has been really inconsistent, if that makes sense. Some days I’ll just forget meals completely, and then other nights I’m up after midnight eating a bunch of takeout or snacks. That’s the part that made me worry, more than my weight being too low.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days lately?

Yeah… I mean, I’ve been trying not to make a big deal out of it, but I guess I have felt pretty down most days. It’s been maybe around four months? The guilt and just not really caring about stuff has kind of been there, and it got harder to brush off after the trouble at work. I don’t know if that’s the right way to describe it, but… yeah, lately it’s been there a lot.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I guess I have. I don’t want it to sound like I’m just being lazy, but things I normally like don’t really pull me in anymore. I used to play soccer on weekends, cook for my girlfriend, go look at little galleries, even help the newer sales guys at work… and lately I just can’t make myself care about any of it. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yeah… a bit. I don’t want to exaggerate it, but at work I’ll be entering an order and then my phone buzzes, or there’s a truck outside, or even someone just walking past the office, and I get pulled off track way more than I should. Then I’ll realize I missed some basic detail I normally would’ve caught. Is that what you mean by trouble concentrating?
Have you had less appetite than usual lately?

Yeah… I mean, not exactly just less, I guess. It’s kind of embarrassing, but it’s been all over the place. Some days I’ll realize I basically forgot to eat, and then other nights I’m up after midnight going through takeout or snacks like I can’t stop. That’s probably not great, right?
Have you been feeling hopeless lately?

Yeah… I guess I have, at least some. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I keep replaying every mistake I made with those Providence accounts and thinking I blew my whole future. Like… I’m useless, and everybody at work can see it. Is that what you mean by hopeless?
Have you had thoughts that you’d be better off dead or of hurting yourself?

I mean… not like I’m planning anything. I don’t want you to think I’m going to do something. But yeah, I’ve had thoughts like… it’d be nice if I could just not wake up for a while, just not have to deal with anything. I haven’t made a plan to hurt myself or anything like that.
Have these symptoms been making it hard for you to function at work or in your daily life?

A little, yeah… I mean, I’m still going in and trying to keep things normal. But my manager’s started taking me off some accounts because I’ve been making mistakes I wouldn’t usually make. And HR got involved after that employee-assistance call, which was… kind of embarrassing.

At home it’s not like everything’s fallen apart, but it feels like I’m barely keeping up. Like work and home are both starting to slip out of my control, if that makes sense.
When this late-night eating happens, have you usually already fallen asleep and then woken up to eat?

Not usually like I’m asleep and then waking up specifically to eat, no. It’s more like I’m already up too late, and then I realize I haven’t eaten much that day, or I just start going through takeout and snacks after midnight.

I know that probably sounds kind of irresponsible… but honestly my eating’s just been really all over the place lately. Some days I basically forget meals, and then other nights it’s like I’m making up for it. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

patient.answer: Yeah… I guess I have, at least some. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I keep replaying every mistake I made with those Providence accounts and thinking I blew my whole future. Like… I’m useless, and everybody at work can see it. Is that what you mean by hopeless?

doctor.intent: Assess for suicidal ideation to clarify depressive episode severity and immediate safety risk.
doctor.question: Have you had thoughts that you’d be better off dead or of hurting yourself?

target_item.name: Death_Suicide
target_item.manifestation: I've had these thoughts where I wish I could just not wake up for a while, but I haven't made a plan to hurt myself.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question directly asks about thoughts of being better off dead or hurting oneself, which matches suicidal ideation and recurrent thoughts of death.

patient.answer: I mean… not like I’m planning anything. I don’t want you to think I’m going to do something. But yeah, I’ve had thoughts like… it’d be nice if I could just not wake up for a while, just not have to deal with anything. I haven’t made a plan to hurt myself or anything like that.

inference.note: This turn added clear evidence for a major depressive episode: depressed mood ~4 months, anhedonia, impaired concentration, appetite disturbance, hopelessness, and passive death wishes without plan. BED remains possible because of recurrent loss-of-control overeating without compensatory behaviors, but the 3-month frequency/duration criterion is still not confirmed, so other/unspecified feeding or eating disorder remain in the differential. Anxiety remains possible but is less central.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the depressive syndrome has caused functional impairment, to better distinguish a major depressive episode from a nonspecific anxiety/eating disorder presentation.
doctor.question: Have these symptoms been making it hard for you to function at work or in your daily life?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: My manager has started pulling me off accounts because I’m making mistakes I normally wouldn’t, and HR got involved after the employee-assistance call. I’m still showing up, but work and home both feel like they’re slipping out of my control.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the symptoms are causing impairment in work or daily life, which directly matches the functional impairment item.

patient.answer:
A little, yeah… I mean, I’m still going in and trying to keep things normal. But my manager’s started taking me off some accounts because I’ve been making mistakes I wouldn’t usually make. And HR got involved after that employee-assistance call, which was… kind of embarrassing.

At home it’s not like everything’s fallen apart, but it feels like I’m barely keeping up. Like work and home are both starting to slip out of my control, if that makes sense.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the eating episodes occur after falling asleep, which would help distinguish night eating syndrome from binge-eating disorder or eating disturbance secondary to depression.
doctor.question: When this late-night eating happens, have you usually already fallen asleep and then woken up to eat?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: Honestly, the thing that scared me into coming in is my eating has been all over the place, like some days I forget meals completely and other nights I'm tearing through takeout and snacks after midnight.
target_item.reason: The question is specifically about late-night eating patterns, which directly relates to appetite and eating changes.

patient.answer:
Not usually like I’m asleep and then waking up specifically to eat, no. It’s more like I’m already up too late, and then I realize I haven’t eaten much that day, or I just start going through takeout and snacks after midnight.

I know that probably sounds kind of irresponsible… but honestly my eating’s just been really all over the place lately. Some days I basically forget meals, and then other nights it’s like I’m making up for it. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking psychiatric care today
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for a moderate depressive episode: depressed mood most days for about four months, loss of interest, concentration problems, appetite disturbance, hopelessness/guilt, passive death wishes, and clear functional impairment at work and home. Although binge-type eating episodes are present, binge eating disorder is not confirmed because the required duration of at least 3 months was not established. No compensatory behaviors were reported, and there is no evidence of low weight. Anxiety symptoms were not the primary syndrome described.
